items.question: How is the hidden-test share rounded when the bounty times the share does not divide evenly?
items.ticket: record a partial release of the configured hidden-test share (default 75%)
items.chose: Rounds the hidden-test amount down with integer division and gives the leftover unit to the UAT part.
items.instead: Round to the nearest unit, or round up.

items.question: What happens when UAT is approved before the hidden tests have passed?
items.ticket: When the maintainer approves UAT on the merge-back PR, release the remaining escrow balance.
items.chose: Throws an error and records nothing.
items.instead: Release the whole bounty, or ignore the event without an error.

items.question: What happens when a hidden-tests-passed event arrives again after the release was already made, whether it is a duplicate delivery or a new event?
items.chose: Releases nothing more, writes nothing to the store, and returns the current state. This is keyed on the release kind, not the event id.
items.instead: Throw an error on the repeat, or deduplicate by event id.

items.question: What happens when a repeated uat-approved event arrives?
items.ticket: Remaining balance is released exactly once
items.chose: Silently returns the current state and writes nothing.
items.instead: Throw an error on the duplicate approval.

items.question: How is the amount of the UAT release worked out?
items.chose: Sets it to the bounty minus the sum of all earlier releases, which is not the stored split.uat figure.

items.question: What happens when a hidden-test run fails after an earlier pass?
items.chose: Ignores the failure. The earlier release stays, and no store write happens.
items.instead: Revoke or flag the earlier release, or throw an error.

items.question: What status does a task with a zero bounty show?
items.ticket: Task shows the bounty as fully released
items.chose: Reports the status as "pro bono" in every case, even after UAT approval.
items.instead: Report "fully released" once UAT is approved, or record no status change.

items.question: How does the handler treat invalid bounty or share values: negative, fractional, above 100%, or beyond the safe-integer range?
items.chose: Throws a RangeError when the handler is created, and also when splitBounty is called.
items.instead: Clamp the values, or reject only when an event is handled.

items.question: What happens when a share of 100% (10000 bps) is configured?
items.chose: Allows it. The first release is the full bounty, and the status is "fully released" straight away.
items.instead: Reject a 100% share, or require UAT approval before the status shows fully released.

items.question: How are events that arrive at the same moment handled?
items.chose: Runs events one at a time through a promise queue. A failed event does not block the ones queued behind it.
items.instead: Use no serialization and rely on the store for atomicity, or use optimistic locking.

items.question: What does the handler do when the store has no state yet, or when a store write fails?
items.chose: Starts from a locked state with no releases. A store write error is passed to the caller and nothing is recorded, so the event can be retried.
items.instead: Throw an error on missing state, or swallow store errors.

items.question: What happens when an event has an unknown kind?
items.chose: Throws an error naming the unknown kind.
items.instead: Ignore the event and return the current state.
